scenes.headline: How a language model reads a prompt it never sees
scenes.sub: Recursive Language Models: context as a variable, recursion as a function call.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Finch! A normal agent works through one growing transcript. A Recursive Language Model replaces that transcript with a Python REPL.

scenes.text: Hold the long prompt as a variable in a Python REPL, let the model slice it with code, and make calling another model an ordinary function.
scenes.say: The idea: hold the prompt as a variable, let the model slice it with code, and make calling another model an ordinary function call.

left.title: In the context window
items: Everything is read into the transcript
Each tool call is a round trip
left.say: Normally, anything the model acts on must be read into its window, and GPT-5's window stops at two hundred and seventy-two thousand tokens.

right.title: In a REPL variable
items: The prompt is bound to a name
Code slices, filters and searches it
Only what is printed enters context
right.say: Here the prompt is a variable. The model writes code to search it, and only what it prints enters its context.

steps.say: The root model never gets the prompt as tokens. It gets its length and a prefix, and a REPL where the prompt already sits.
It writes code that slices and searches the prompt. The REPL runs it, and only truncated output comes back.

steps.note: recursion depth is capped in code
steps.say: To delegate, it calls another model like any function, on a snippet. The result is a value, so a for loop can fan out.
It repeats until it calls FINAL with its answer.

scenes.title: RLM around GPT-5: median gain over each baseline
scenes.note: single paper, not yet independently replicated
scenes.say: Wrapped this way, GPT-5 beat CodeAct with sub-calls by a median hundred and thirty percent. CodeAct runs code too. The difference is where the input lives.

scenes.text: An RLM doesn't optimize the agent loop. It moves the task's state out of the transcript and into an interpreter.

recap: The prompt is a variable, not tokens
Code decides what the model reads
Calling a model is a function call
scenes.say: To recap: the prompt is a variable, code decides what gets read, and a sub-model is just a function call.
